subject: Concession structure for unpredictable spikes + rebaseline mechanics
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@nexahealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@nexahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected monthly spike — renewal planning question

Hi Sofia / Jordan,

Quick background: we saw a ~4x spike in token consumption for 48 hours during a campaign in Oct. Our engineering team has mitigations, but given the renewal window coming up in December we need to discuss three things: 1) an operational "grace" or buffer for one-off spikes so we don't get penalized with high overage bills, 2) an agreed rebaseline cadence so our committed tier can be adjusted without a full contract redline, and 3) a cap on Year-2 uplift that protects our budget.

Can Redwood propose an approach that preserves your unit economics but gives us predictable cost exposure for bursty events? We prefer a short pilot for the concession mechanics rather than a permanent permanent price change.

Attaching our usage export for Q3 so you can see the pattern (usage-history-2026Q3.csv).

Thanks — happy to hop on a call this week if helpful.

— Alex
Director, AI Platforms
Nexa Health

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected monthly spike — renewal planning question

Alex — thanks for the context and the CSV.

High-level proposal (pilot-first):
- Grace band: allow a one-time quarterly "grace" of up to 150% of committed monthly tokens where overage is credited back as a one-time account credit (not a price change). This credit is reconciled at the next invoice.
- Spike trigger & verification: spikes flagged automatically (1.5x baseline across >=24h) and verified with usage logs (you provided Q3 — helpful).
- Rebaseline cadence: 90-day rebaseline window post-renewal (one-sided rebaseline request from customer; Redwood can approve one rebaseline in the first 12 months to avoid frequent churn).
- Year-2 uplift cap: limit automatic renewal uplift to +20% year-over-year unless both sides agree to a higher commit.
- Rollback path: if actual sustained usage falls >30% below committed level for 2 consecutive months after rebaseline, customer can request a tier rollback (subject to 30-day notice).

I've attached a short outline of the mechanics (spike-protection-outline.pdf) and included the internal pricing owners on Cc to tune numbers. If this structure looks reasonable we can convert it into an SOW addendum and DocuSign-ready language.

Next steps: confirm whether Nexa wants the pilot to be 90 or 180 days, and whether credits should be applied automatically or on mutual review.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected monthly spike — renewal planning question

Sofia / Marissa — thoughts from pricing/ops:
- Grace band sizing: 150% for a single monthly window is probably defensible for a pilot. If we see repeated usage >2x within the pilot window, convert to an overage rate at a slightly higher per-token price (we should define that ceiling).
- Credits: apply automatically to the invoice but cap total credits for the pilot at 25% of annual committed spend to protect Redwood economics.
- Rebaseline approval: require a short justification (product campaign, new feature rollout) + two weeks of post-spike telemetry before we accept a rebaseline. This prevents gaming.
- Rollback: allow a single rollback in first 12 months; require 30-day notice as Sofia suggested.

I'll draft the pricing table and the fallback floor for the per-token overage rate (propose 1.8x current effective per-token) and send to legal to bake into the addendum.

Karthik
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@nexahealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@nexahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected monthly spike — renewal planning question

Thanks — this is very helpful and closer to what we had in mind. A couple quick confirmations before we proceed: 1) Pilot length: we prefer 180 days, 2) Credits: automatic application is fine as long as we get a clear line item on the invoice, 3) Can you confirm the proposed annual credit cap in dollars so our procurement team can sign off?

If the cap is acceptable we'll need a short SOW addendum + a DocuSign envelope we can route internally (our legal is fast). Also: can you include an explicit data-retention clause for usage logs used in verification? That's important for our security/compliance team.

If you can get a draft SOW/DocuSign over early next week we can expedite the renewal.

— Alex
Director, AI Platforms, Nexa Health
